summary: Backend fully passing (9/9 pytest). Front Porch PIN gate works (both the 'Tap for Guest PIN' auto-unlock and manual keypad PIN entry unlock the dashboard with navigation tabs: Home, Family Albums, Today's Plan, Recipes, Scripture, Thoughts). Stripe checkout API returns valid Stripe hosted-checkout URL with correct $40/yr pricing, metadata and session_id; redirect from the SubscriptionModal into Stripe's hosted page works end-to-end. Full completion of payment on Stripe hosted checkout could not be reliably automated in 3 attempts — all fields (email, 4242 card, 12/34, CVC 123, cardholder, US address, phone) were filled and the Subscribe button clicked, but the Stripe page remained on the checkout URL with no navigation back to /payment/success. This is almost certainly due to Stripe sandbox's 'This page is from an unclaimed Stripe sandbox' banner + the Link 'Save my information' flow requiring real phone/email verification (not a Hearth code bug). Backend provisioning path from payment metadata is implemented correctly and verified via the direct POST /api/tenants path. Recommend main agent either (a) manually complete one real Stripe sandbox checkout to confirm /payment/success provisioning, or (b) add STRIPE_PAYMENT_METHOD_TYPES=['card'] and disable Link auto-signup on the Checkout Session to make automated QA easier.

integration_issues.issue: Could not programmatically complete Stripe hosted checkout in automated test (Link signup + unclaimed-sandbox banner). Redirect to Stripe works and metadata is correct; the return/provision step was not executed end-to-end from the browser. Everything up to Stripe is confirmed working.

server.py: GET /api/tenants/{slug} correctly omits familyPinHash via safe_tenant() and exposes hasPinSet. Verified.
server.py: Uses `stripe.error.InvalidRequestError` which still works but is deprecated in newer stripe-python; consider `stripe.InvalidRequestError`.
server.py seed_tenants runs on every import — fine but should guard against race in multi-worker environments.
SubscriptionModal.tsx: inputs lack data-testid attributes (sanctuary-name, slug, owner-email, family-pin, continue-btn, subscribe-launch-btn). Would make automated QA deterministic.
PaymentSuccessView has good data-testids already (enter-sanctuary-btn, copy-owner-link-btn, public-bio-link, payment-success-view) — good.
